native_result.query: In which century did summed social capital peak, what individual social capital components like gold, monument etc increase?
native_result.HypoA: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?
native_result.HypoB: Summed social capital peaked in the 14th century BCE (1400–1300 BCE, Older Bronze Age) at a value of 4.238, driven by major increases in Copper and Gold (from -0.36 to +2.54) and Monument Count (from +0.17 to +1.71), alongside a modest rise in Amber (from -0.15 to -0.01).
native_result.WorkflowB: Loaded and normalized capital.csv and time_series_data.csv, computed summed social capital as ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument across 4300–500 BCE, located maximum value and corresponding century bins, and quantified component-level delta between 1500 BCE and the peak at 1400–1300 BCE.

sub_hypo.text: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monument Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneously while summer social capital peaks.
sub_hypo.relations: Monument Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneously while summer social capital peaks; no column corresponding to summer social capital is identified.

gold_sub_hypo.full_hypo: From 1500 BCE onwards, Monuments Count and Copper & Gold increase simultaneuosly while summer social capital peaks?

sub_hypo.text: Summed social capital peaked in the 14th century BCE (1400–1300 BCE, Older Bronze Age) at 4.238, driven by major increases in Copper and Gold and Monument Count, alongside a modest rise in Amber.
sub_hypo.context: Archaeological capital data across 4300–500 BCE, with the peak in 1400–1300 BCE (Older Bronze Age) and component changes measured relative to 1500 BCE.
sub_hypo.relations: Summed social capital, computed as ZCU_AU + Zamber + ZMonument, reached its maximum of 4.238 in 1400–1300 BCE. From 1500 BCE to the peak, Copper and Gold increased from -0.36 to +2.54 (delta +2.90), Monument Count increased from +0.17 to +1.71 (delta +1.54), and Amber increased modestly from -0.15 to -0.01 (delta +0.14).

gen_sub_hypo.full_hypo: Summed social capital peaked in the 14th century BCE (1400–1300 BCE, Older Bronze Age) at a value of 4.238, driven by major increases in Copper and Gold (from -0.36 to +2.54) and Monument Count (from +0.17 to +1.71), alongside a modest rise in Amber (from -0.15 to -0.01).
